course_summary:
ISEN 635 | Human Information Processing | Fall 2026
Instructor: Thomas Ferris | tferris@tamu.edu
Grading: Homework [30%], Exams [50%], Semester project [20%] (proposal [1%], written report [10%], project presentation [9%]) — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89%, C: 70-79%, D: 60-69%, F: 59% and lower
Topics: Neuropsychological processes, man-machine systems design, psychophysiological methods, multiple resources theory, cognitive systems engineering, user-centered design principles, human-centered redesign solutions, peer-reviews, Vigilance, Visual processing, color vision, object recognition, depth perception, Audition, Timesharing, Haptics, haptic communication, Multisensory processing, Multimodal interfaces, central processes, decision making, human component, information processor, models of basic cognitive functions, pattern recognition, attention, memory, human-systems analysis, design methods, neuroanatomy, sensory physiology, cognitive psychology, philosophy, signal detection theory, information theory, mental workload assessment, existing technology evaluation, redesign solutions, communication skills, quantitative engineering methods, psychophysics, hot topics, trends, human information processing research, technical works review, human data collection, human performance assessment, cognitive workload assessment, real world task, creativity, human-systems interaction problems, quantitative problem exercises, reading responses, Information processing model, Sensation, Perception, Vision, Learning, Design for supporting Human Information Processing, Usability, interaction
Tools: Canvas
Prerequisites: ISEN 430 or approval of instructor
